$comment: Machine-readable style profiles. Human-facing rationale lives in reference/style-profiles.md. Every colour pair here has been checked against WCAG AA on its own paper; see contrast_checked below.

soft-gradient.label: Soft gradient — light, modern, product-launch register
soft-gradient.use_when: Vertical social, product explainers, anything that should feel current and warm. Big weight contrast, one blue, soft colour fields behind white cards.
soft-gradient.background: Three soft radial fields (one warm, two cool) blurred behind a near-white paper, plus a static dither grain. See reference/style-profiles.md.

contrast_checked.note: Checked worst-case: every text colour against the paper AND against each colour field at full strength. soft started at #5f6367 and measured 4.08:1 on the warm field — scripts/check_contrast.py caught it and #585c60 is the corrected value. A pale grey label straight from reference imagery lands near 2.1:1.

editorial-paper.label: Editorial paper — calm, printed, technical-documentation register
editorial-paper.use_when: Landscape explainers, architecture and decision diagrams, anything that should read as a considered figure in a printed essay.

motion.character: measured, deliberate, one gesture at a time

editorial-paper.background: Flat paper. Optional 22px dot grid at 10% ink. No colour fields.

contrast_checked.note: soft is corrected from the upstream #7a8399, which measures 3.48:1 and fails AA. accent (#eb6c36) measures 2.86:1 as text and is stroke-only; accent-ink is its text-safe counterpart.

geometry.$comment_viewbox: Author in viewBox units, render at 2x. Every coordinate divisible by the grid.

budget.$comment: Per figure, not per canvas. Two figures side by side each get their own budget.

$rule_accent: accent is for strokes and fills. accent-text is the only accent value allowed on type. In editorial-paper they differ because the orange measures 2.86:1 as text; in soft-gradient they happen to coincide. Always reference accent-text for type so a profile swap cannot break the gate.
